who: Historian of architecture at Université Laval; PhD MIT, 1991.

evidence.says: Names Marc Grignon of Université Laval as co-director of Agueda Iturbe-Kennedy’s thesis; records its defense in 2017.
Identifies the Laval art-history professor, his MIT PhD (1991), and his book Loing du Soleil on architecture in Quebec.
Authority for Marc Grignon cites Loing du soleil and L’art de l’architecte, matching the Laval scholar’s works.

notes: Institution, named student and publications identify the match. The thesis source gives 2017 rather than the AHA entry’s 2019.

who: Donald Finlay Davis, historian of urban and automotive history at the University of Ottawa.

evidence.says: The abstract of Ruth Dunley’s 2008 Ottawa thesis A.D. Smith: Knight-Errant of Radical Democracy names Dr. Donald F. Davis as supervisor.
Publisher identifies Conspicuous Production’s author as Donald Finlay Davis, Associate Professor of History at the University of Ottawa.
The Donald Finlay Davis authority cites Conspicuous production (1988).

notes: The student’s supervisor name and institution connect to the full name and work in the supplied authority.

who: Gerald Neil (Gary) Knoppers, Hebrew Bible scholar at Penn State before moving to Notre Dame in 2014; PhD Harvard.

evidence.says: Kenneth Ristau states that he completed his Penn State PhD in 2013 under Dr. Gary Knoppers.
Identifies Gerald Neil Knoppers as Gary Knoppers, with a Harvard doctorate and 25 years teaching at Penn State before Notre Dame in 2014.
Authority for Gerald Neil Knoppers cites What share have we in David? (1988).
The indexed institutional CV identifies Gerald Neil Knoppers’s 1988 Harvard dissertation as What Share Have We in David?: The Division of the Kingdom in Kings and Chronicles.

notes: Direct student testimony confirms supervision; the full name and dissertation connect the LC authority. The CV is indexed but its current URL returns 404.

who: Professor of English and women’s and gender studies at Drew University, specializing in Victorian literature and feminist theory.

evidence.says: Drew identifies Wendy Kolmar as its professor of English and women’s and gender studies and lists Haunting the House of Fiction among her publications.
The 2005–2006 Caspersen School faculty directory lists Wendy Kolmar in English, establishing her Drew appointment in the relevant period.
Authority for Wendy K. Kolmar cites Haunting the house of fiction (1991).

notes: The institutional affiliation, period, field and matching publication support the authority match; individual dissertation supervision was not independently located.

who: Raymond T. McNally, historian of Russian intellectual life at Boston College, 1958–1999; doctorate at the Free University of Berlin.

evidence.says: AHA memorial by Nicholas S. Racheotes describes McNally’s Berlin doctorate, Boston College appointment from 1958 to 1999, and graduate thesis direction in Russian intellectual history.
Authority for Raymond T. McNally explicitly identifies Boston College in its citation for Philosophical works of Peter Chaadaev (1991).

notes: The authority explicitly supplies the correct institution; the field and appointment cover both students’ dissertation years.

who: Karl John Seitz, history dissertation supervisor at the University of New Mexico in the 1970s.

evidence.says: UNM’s record for Stephen Merle Fuller’s dissertation names Karl John Seitz as committee chair; the repository dates it 1974.
Karlheinz Seitz is identified as a physician in Sigmaringen and author of Sonografie kompetent.
Karl Seitz is identified as mayor of Vienna and president of Austria.

notes: Both supplied authorities identify different people. Fuller’s repository date differs from the AHA year, but the title and chair establish the supervisor’s identity.

who: Historian of Latin American political thought at Fordham University, also known as Carlos Otto Stoetzer.

evidence.says: Fordham names O. Carlos Stoetzer as mentor for Delma S. Arrigoitia’s 1985 dissertation and Bruce Taylor’s 1973 dissertation, with the titles in the AHA entry.
The Ibero-Amerikanisches Institut identifies Carlos Otto Stoetzer as a historian and political scientist who taught at Fordham and wrote on Latin American history and politics.
The authority is headed Stoetzer, O. Carlos and cites his Postage stamps as propaganda (1953).

notes: Exact distinctive name and direct confirmation of both students at Fordham support the supplied authority match.

who: Listed by AHA as a University of Southern California doctoral supervisor in 1973–1974; independent identity unresolved.

evidence.says: Cites Kaye Lynn Briegel’s Alianza Hispano-Americana, 1894–1965 as a USC PhD dissertation from 1974, but does not identify its supervisor.
One supplied Margaret Williams authority cites The Jews among the Greeks and Romans (1998); it supplies no USC affiliation or connection to these students.
